title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page differs from its neighbours. The surrounding pages are handwritten notes on p-adic Hodge-type fibre functors, torsors P under G_L and the Hodge cocharacters (i_1, i_2). This page is a typed sheet, numbered 34, from a text on étale cohomological purity and the cohomology class of a cycle. It references (IX 3.2), the Kummer sequence of SGA 4 IX, plus internal numbers (3.1), (3.8), (3.10)(iii) and (3.10.1). The style and setting fit the purity / fundamental-class material of SGA 4 (Exposés XVI and XIX) or a related draft; the exact source is unsure.

Setting, in modern terms: X is a regular scheme (from context, of equal characteristic p, or strictly local), and n is prime to p. Y is a regular divisor (codimension c = 1) with complement j: U → X. The aim is the base case of absolute cohomological purity: the isomorphism R^1 j_* μ_n ≅ (Z/n)_Y.

Step 1. X is regular, so it is locally factorial. Every invertible sheaf on U therefore extends to X, which gives R^1 j_* G_m = 0.

Step 2. Apply j_* to the Kummer sequence 0 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 0 on U. Since R^1 j_* G_m = 0, this gives (*): (j_* G_m)/n ≅ R^1 j_* μ_n.

Step 3. There is the divisor sequence 0 → G_{m,X} → j_* G_{m,U} → Z_Y → 0. The map to Z_Y is the order of vanishing along Y, normalised so that a local equation t maps to 1.

Step 4. Reduce this sequence mod n. G_{m,X} is n-divisible étale-locally because n is invertible, and Z_Y has no n-torsion. Hence (j_* G_m)/n ≅ (Z/n)_Y. Combined with (*), this gives R^1 j_* μ_n ≅ (Z/n)_Y, i.e. the class of a regular divisor (purity in codimension 1).

Step 5. The text then starts the induction on the codimension c > 1. Assume existence and uniqueness of the classes / purity isomorphisms in codimension < c. Using (3.8), the three maps of (3.10.1), namely φ(Z,Y), ξ and η, are étale-local and commute with base change. These are presumably the transitivity maps for a flag Z ⊂ Y ⊂ X. This is the standard dévissage of the purity statement for regular pairs.
errors: No mathematical error. In the divisor sequence, the identification of Z_Y with the valuation needs Y to be a regular divisor, hence locally irreducible; that is implicit in the setting. The mod-n step tacitly uses étale-local n-divisibility of G_m (n invertible) and the absence of torsion in Z_Y; both are fine.
Typographic slips in the original: 'Il s'ensuite', 'recurrence', 'démontrés' (should be 'démontrées'), and 'déjà définis' for 'flèches' (feminine).

ideas.what: R^1 j_* G_m = 0 for the complement of a divisor in a regular (locally factorial) scheme, hence R^1 j_* μ_n ≅ (j_* G_m)/n via Kummer
ideas.modern_name: Codimension-1 case of absolute cohomological purity / cycle class of a divisor
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exposés IX, XVI, XIX (purity in codimension 1); SGA 4½ Cycle

ideas.what: Induction on codimension for existence and uniqueness of purity isomorphisms, using étale-local nature and base-change compatibility of the transitivity maps φ(Z,Y), ξ, η
ideas.modern_name: Purity for regular pairs; Gysin transitivity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Artin (SGA 4 XIX, equal characteristic); later Gabber (absolute purity)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 XIX §3 (likely the source draft; unsure)

missed.claim: Archival note: this typed page of an SGA-style purity text (page 34) is filed in the middle of the handwritten 'Cristaux' notes on p-adic Hodge / Tannakian torsors. It is probably a reused sheet or a misfiled page, not part of the crystal argument.
missed.quote: Supposons maintenant que l'existence et unicité sont déjà démontrés si la codimension est < c
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only relevant for cataloguing the archive and dating SGA 4 XIX-type drafts. There is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard codimension-1 purity computation and the start of the codimension induction, as in SGA 4. It is routine and published. The only oddity is that it is a misfiled typed page.
transcription_corrections: In the second isomorphism, a struck-out symbol (possibly φ) precedes (Z/n)_Y. The target is simply (Z/n)_Y.
The deleted reference before (3.10.1) is a typed-over duplicate of '(3.10.1)'.
'commutent aux changement de base' is the typed original ('commutent' overstruck from 'commutent/commutet').
